answer: A hardware-rooted attestation protocol limits Sybil attacks by binding each agent to a secure enclave that generates verifiable cryptographic quotes. To survive a gale of synthetic clones, each peer submits an umber identity token authenticated across an operational validation trellis. An attacker must acquire scarce, authentic physical security chips per rogue identity. However, undetected microarchitectural side-channel vulnerabilities can permit counterfeit enclave signatures.
